cohort: The study included placentas from 50 COVID-19-positive pregnant females and 50 term historical placentas as controls.
finding: Maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection was significantly associated with placental histopathological changes, predominantly chorangiosis (56% of cases) indicating fetal vascular malperfusion, along with other features like maternal vascular malperfusions and intervillous fibrinoid deposition.
cross-section timing: Immediately post-birth, on placentas from pregnancies that reached term, collected between August 2020 to October 2020.
